title: Year four close
hook: law, thought, streams, character, life and language
tomorrow: Year five opens: the sources themselves

segments.voice: Yesterday, a verse alone: bereshit bara Elohim, read by yourself, word by word. Your line was bereshit bara. Did you begin something with it? Today is the last day of year four. Day one thousand four hundred twenty-six.

A man comes to Hillel with a dare: teach me the whole Torah while I stand on one foot. The Talmud says Shammai had already sent him away. Hillel doesn't. He gives him one sentence: what is hateful to you, do not do to your neighbor. That is the whole Torah, he says, and the rest is commentary. And then two more words, easy to skip past: go and learn. This whole year has been the go and learn. Not the one sentence, but the long commentary that grew around it, the way Jews argue, decide, pray, mourn, celebrate, and speak. Today, the year in one look.
screen: `TEACH ME ON ONE FOOT.` → `THE REST IS COMMENTARY.` → `GO AND LEARN.`

segments.voice: Year four close. The year opened with a promise: now, how it works. Here's how it went, in six words. First, law. The Mishnah and the Talmud, the oral Torah set down, page after page of rabbis disagreeing on the record, and the codes that turned argument into practice. The block closed with the Talmud called a sea: nobody crosses it, but everyone can swim. Second, thought. Maimonides, the physician and philosopher who argued that reason can serve faith. Then the hidden side: Kabbalah and the Hasidic masters, sparks scattered in the world and a light from creation kept hidden away. Third, streams. Orthodox, Conservative, Reform, Reconstructionist, Renewal, secular and more, each described in its own terms and ranked against none. Many streams, one river. Fourth, character, life and language. Mussar taught that the traits are built one ordinary day at a time. The life cycle walked from a baby's naming to a wedding canopy to a mourner's kaddish. And these last weeks, the roots: letters that turn out to be numbers, a break that holds a birth, a name that opens a book, and a single verse you read by yourself. Put the six together and you get the year's line. Judaism isn't only something believed. It's a way of thinking, out loud and in pairs, and a way of living, at the table and the door and the graveside. That's why Hillel didn't stop at his one sentence: go and learn. Judaism thinks and lives.
screen: `LAW: THE SEA OF TALMUD.` · `THOUGHT: REASON AND HIDDEN LIGHT.` · `STREAMS: MANY, ONE RIVER.` · `CHARACTER, LIFE AND LANGUAGE.` · then, large: `JUDAISM THINKS AND LIVES.`

segments.voice: Here's today's practice: say a blessing for understanding. Sit, and let your breath slow. Let the year pass in front of you: one argument from the Talmud that stuck, one teacher, one trait you worked on, one Hebrew root. Just one of each, if they come. In the weekday Amidah, the standing prayer, there is a blessing that asks God for knowledge, understanding and discernment, and it closes by blessing God, who graciously grants knowledge. If you pray, you can say that blessing now, from a siddur, in Hebrew or in English. If you don't, sit with the plain wish behind it: to understand a little more next year than this one. The bell holds the time.
screen: `ONE ARGUMENT, ONE TEACHER.` · `ONE TRAIT, ONE ROOT.` · `A BLESSING FOR UNDERSTANDING.`

segments.voice: Year four close. How Judaism thinks and lives: law, thought, streams, character, life and language. Today's word.

notes: Shabbat 31a paraphrased: the would-be convert first goes to Shammai, who pushes him away with a builder's measuring stick; Hillel answers 'what is hateful to you, do not do to your fellow; that is the whole Torah, the rest is its commentary; go and learn'. Confirm paraphrase.
